note: Ask knowledge base for nvs.ide. Each entry answers one 'how do I...' question. 'q' holds phrasings and keywords used for matching; 'keys' is the Vim way, 'vscode' is what the user probably already knows, 'try' is an optional Ex command the Ask window can run for the user.

entries.a: Press Esc to be sure you're in Normal mode, then type :q and Enter. :wq saves first, :q! throws away changes, and :qa quits everything.

Vim has modes. Normal mode is for moving and editing commands, Insert mode is for typing text, and Visual mode is for selecting. The status bar shows which one you're in. i enters Insert mode and Esc goes back to Normal.
From Normal mode, press i to type before the cursor, a to type after it, A to type at the end of the line, I at the start, o to open a new line below and O above.
entries.keys: i a A I o O

entries.a: Press Esc. If Esc feels far away, turn on 'jk leaves Insert mode' in Settings > Transition, then type j and k quickly.
Type :w and Enter. In nvs.ide, Ctrl+S also saves at every stage, because LazyVim maps it. :wa saves every open file.
Type :wa and Enter to write every changed file.
Press Space Space (or Space f f) to fuzzy-find a file in the project, like Ctrl+P in VS Code. Type part of the name and press Enter.
Space f r lists recently opened files.
Space e toggles the file explorer. Inside it, j and k move, l or Enter opens, h closes a folder, a creates a file, d deletes and r renames.
Type :e followed by the new file name, like :e notes.md, then save with :w. In the explorer (Space e), press a.
Open the explorer with Space e, put the cursor on the file and press r.
Space b d closes the current buffer (Vim's word for an open file). Space b o closes all the others.
Shift+L goes to the next open file and Shift+H to the previous one. Space , lists all open buffers.
Harpoon keeps a short list of files you jump between. Space H adds the current file, Space h opens the list, and Space 1 to Space 9 jump straight to a slot.
h moves left, j down, k up and l right. Put a number first to repeat: 5j moves five lines down. The relative line numbers on the left tell you that number.
w jumps to the start of the next word, b back to the previous word, and e to the end of the word.
0 goes to the very start of the line, ^ to the first non-blank character, and $ to the end.
gg goes to the first line and G to the last.
Type the number then G (42G), or type :42 and Enter.
Ctrl+D scrolls half a page down and Ctrl+U half a page up. Ctrl+F and Ctrl+B move a full page, except at Stages 1 to 3 where those keep their VS Code meaning.

q: go back to where i was
entries.a: Ctrl+O jumps back to where you were and Ctrl+I jumps forward again.
% jumps to the bracket, brace or parenthesis matching the one under the cursor.

q: jump to a word i can see
entries.a: Press s, then type the first two letters of where you want to go. Labels appear on every match; press the label to jump. This comes from flash.nvim.
x deletes the character under the cursor. 3x deletes three.
dd deletes the current line. 3dd deletes three lines. What you delete is kept, so p pastes it back somewhere else.
dw deletes from the cursor to the start of the next word. diw deletes the whole word the cursor is on.
D (or d$) deletes from the cursor to the end of the line.
ciw deletes the word under the cursor and puts you in Insert mode to type the new one. The same idea works with other targets: ci" changes inside quotes, ci( inside parentheses.
r then a character replaces the one under the cursor without entering Insert mode.
u undoes the last change. At Stages 1 to 3, Ctrl+Z works too.
Ctrl+R redoes what u undid.
. (a dot) repeats your last change. Change one word with ciw, move to another and press . to change it the same way.
yy copies the current line. p pastes it below and P above. yyp duplicates a line in one go.
Select with v, then press y to copy. nvs.ide shares the system clipboard, so Ctrl+V in other apps pastes it.
p pastes after the cursor and P before it. In Insert mode, Ctrl+R then + pastes the system clipboard.
Alt+J moves the current line (or selection) down and Alt+K moves it up.
>> indents the line and << unindents it. In Visual mode, > and < shift the selection and keep it selected.
J joins the next line onto the end of this one.
~ flips the case of the character under the cursor. In Visual mode, U makes the selection uppercase and u lowercase.
gcc comments or uncomments the current line. In Visual mode, gc does the selection. At Stages 1 to 3, Ctrl+/ works as well.
gsa adds a surround (gsaiw" wraps the word in quotes), gsd deletes one and gsr replaces one. This comes from mini.surround.

Vim does this differently. For a column, press Ctrl+V, select down with j, then I, type, and Esc: the text appears on every line. To change each match of a word, press * on it, then cgn, type, Esc, and press . for each next match.
qa starts recording into register a, q stops. @a plays it back, and 10@a plays it ten times.
v starts selecting character by character, V selects whole lines, and Ctrl+V selects a block (a column). Move to grow the selection, then act on it: d deletes, y copies, c changes.
ggVG selects the whole file: go to the top, start a line selection, go to the bottom.
viw selects the word under the cursor, vi" inside quotes, vi( inside parentheses and vip the paragraph.
Type / then the text and Enter. n goes to the next match and N to the previous. * searches for the word under the cursor.
Space / (or Space s g) searches every file in the project as you type.
Type :%s/old/new/g and Enter to replace every match in the file. Add c at the end (/gc) to confirm each one.
Space s r opens a search-and-replace panel for the whole project (grug-far).
Press Esc in Normal mode. LazyVim clears the search highlight for you.
Space | splits the window side by side and Space - splits it top and bottom. Space w d closes the current split.
Ctrl+H, Ctrl+J, Ctrl+K and Ctrl+L move to the window on the left, below, above and right. The long form is Ctrl+W then h, j, k or l.
Space f t opens a terminal. Inside it you're typing into the shell; press Ctrl+\ then Ctrl+N to get back to Normal mode so you can scroll and copy.
Space s C searches every command. Typing : opens the command line for Ex commands like :w or :set.
Press Space and wait: which-key shows every leader shortcut, grouped. Space s k searches all keymaps.
:h followed by a topic opens Neovim's built-in help, for example :h motion. Space s h searches all help pages.
:NvsTutor opens the nvs.ide lessons, which you practise in a real buffer. :Tutor opens Neovim's own full tutorial.
:NvsStage 1 gives you VS Code keys, 2 is Hybrid, 3 is Modal with a safety net, 4 is pure Neovim. The coach hints go quiet at Stage 4.
gd jumps to the definition of the symbol under the cursor. Ctrl+O brings you back.
gr lists every reference to the symbol under the cursor.
Space c r renames the symbol under the cursor everywhere the language server knows about.
Space c a shows code actions and quick fixes for the cursor position.
K shows the documentation and type of the symbol under the cursor.
Space c f formats the file. LazyVim also formats on save; Space u f turns that off.
]d and [d jump to the next and previous problem. Space x x opens a list of every problem (Trouble). Space c d shows the full message for the current line.

Suggestions appear as you type. Ctrl+N and Ctrl+P (or the arrow keys) move through them, Enter accepts, and Ctrl+Space opens the menu by hand. If local AI is on, grey ghost text shows a longer suggestion; Alt+A accepts it.
Snippets appear in the completion menu with a snippet icon. Accept one with Enter, then Tab jumps to the next placeholder.
za toggles the fold under the cursor, zM closes all folds and zR opens them all.
Space g g opens lazygit, a full git interface: space stages a file, c commits, P pushes. (lazygit has to be installed.)
]h and [h jump between changed blocks, Space g h s stages the block under the cursor and Space g h b shows who last changed the line.
:Lazy opens the plugin manager (U updates everything). :LazyExtras switches on ready-made bundles such as language support. In the nvs.ide window, the Plugins view does the same with buttons.
:LazyExtras has a lang section (lang.python, lang.rust, lang.typescript and more); press x on one to enable it. :Mason installs individual servers, linters and formatters.

:set changes an option for now, for example :set relativenumber! toggles relative numbers. To keep it, add it to lua/config/options.lua, or use the Settings screen in the nvs.ide window, which writes that file for you.
Space u C previews and switches colour schemes. nvs.ide ships with necronomicon.

Turn it on with :NvsAI on. By default nvs.ide runs llama.cpp itself, so any GGUF model works and nothing else is needed. Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server like LM Studio also work (:NvsAI backend ollama). Ask uses the model when no written answer matches, and ghost-text completion uses it for longer suggestions. Everything stays on 127.0.0.1.
Space ? (or F1 at Stages 1 to 3) opens Ask. Type a question in plain words, like 'delete a line' or 'split the screen'.

q: get a model from hugging face
entries.a: :NvsModel pull followed by a Hugging Face repo and quantisation downloads it into the models folder, for example :NvsModel pull Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M. :NvsModel on its own lists your models and picks which one Ask and completion use. You can also drop .gguf files into the folder that :NvsModel folder opens.

Markdown renders right in the editor: headings, lists, tables, checkboxes and code blocks are drawn as you read, and the raw text comes back on the line you're editing. Space u m turns that on and off. Space c p opens a live preview in your browser that scrolls along with the cursor.
